label: History
value: Adrian recovered from typhoid.
unit: After recovering from typhoid, Adrian traveled to Seven Gulls on his doctor's advice to recuperate near the ocean and view his grandparents' original homestead. He stayed as a guest with Lorna Vane and quickly formed a close friendship with Nell Carrow, Dr. Hugh Carrow, and Captain Saul Garrick. Upon discovering Captain Saul's detailed life-book of maritime adventures, Adrian collaborated with him to write a novel based on his life and the tale of lost Margaret. During this summer of creative work and social outings, Adrian fell deeply in love with Lorna, but he kept his feelings secret out of respect for her circumstances until her freedom was clarified. He completed the manuscript in September and returned to Toronto. He later reached out to return for another visit, courting Lorna and eventually becoming engaged to her. Their wedding was set for Christmas, and Adrian purchased the old House of Dreams property from the church trustees for their summer holidays. The publication of their book, The Life-Book of Captain Saul, was met with great satisfaction by Captain Saul. Adrian and Lorna later had children, including Damaris and Julian. In a subsequent summer, Adrian took his family to Japan for a year to gather background material for a new novel.

label: History
value: Agatha Sowerby lived for decades in Brierley.
unit: Agatha Sowerby lived for decades in Brierley, serving as a pillar of the local church organizations, including directing the Sewing Circle and participating in the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. Sitting by her kitchen window in Sowerby's Hollow, she spent hours crafting cotton-warp quilts while observing every traveler along the road. When her longtime neighbor Thirza Abernethy and her brother Obed took in an orphan girl named Nell, Agatha actively expressed her frank opinions and disapproval, though she eventually warmed to Nell and praised her usefulness. Following the death of her husband Thomas Sowerby, Agatha sold her excess household belongings and moved into a reconditioned suite at Grey Shutters to live alongside Thirza. In later years, she continued her involvement in village life, visited Nell and Hugh after their marriage, and spent her remaining years making quilts for Nell's future daughters.

label: History
value: Ambrose Kerr grew up near Seven Gulls.
unit: Ambrose Kerr grew up near Seven Gulls and engaged fiercely in politics as a Liberal partisan. During a bitter general election fifteen years prior to volume 4, he swore publicly that he would not cut his hair or shave his face until the Grits took power. True to his word, he allowed his hair and beard to grow wild for a decade and a half. During this time, he spent his days cod-fishing with Captain Saul, engaging in lively discussions, and entertaining friends like Lorna Ainslie and Nell Harcourt with his stories, tenor ballad singing, and skill at dancing. When the Liberals finally won the election, Ambrose immediately walked to Augustus Palmer's barber shop after midnight and compelled the barber to give him a full haircut and shave. Soon after, he married Miss Winifred Tolley and moved into her home located between the Glen and Seven Gulls Point, surrounding it with planted trees, a spruce hedge, and a rose garden. When he heard of the mistreatment suffered by the orphan Mary Stubbs, his outrage prompted him to investigate the matter across the harbor, and he readily agreed with his wife to adopt Mary into their home.

True to his word, he allowed his hair and beard to grow wild for a decade and a half. During this time, he spent his days cod-fishing with Captain Saul, engaging in lively discussions, and entertaining friends like Lorna Ainslie and Nell Harcourt with his stories, tenor ballad singing, and skill at dancing. When the Liberals finally won the election, Ambrose immediately walked to Augustus Palmer's barber shop after midnight and compelled the barber to give him a full haircut and shave. Soon after, he married Miss Winifred Tolley and moved into her home located between the Glen and Seven Gulls Point, surrounding it with planted trees, a spruce hedge, and a rose garden. When he heard of the mistreatment suffered by the orphan Mary Stubbs, his outrage prompted him to investigate the matter across the harbor, and he readily agreed with his wife to adopt Mary into their home.

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk is an orphan.
unit: Anthony Tulk, an orphaned nephew taken in by Mrs. Laurence Tulk, began attending Brierley school under the instruction of Nell Harcourt. From his arrival, he held a sullen disdain for Nell due to his belief that female teachers were useless. On his first day, he emptied his slate bottle down a girl's neck, and later placed a live mouse in Nell's desk drawer. After admitting to the prank with insolence, Nell lost her temper and gave him a whipping with a wooden pointer. Contrary to Nell's fears that she had lost him forever, the whipping earned Anthony's respect, causing him to offer to carry her books the next morning and remark that she had some worth after all. When Nell eventually resigned as teacher, Anthony engaged in two deliberate fights with other boys to process his emotions.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia moved to Portmaris
unit: After her daughter married and left for the mission field, Aunt Euphemia moved to Portmaris to act as housekeeper for Nell, Honora, Cressy, and Mabel at Tabby's Place. She brought along two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted the stray cat Smudge into her care as well. She spent three winters chaperoning and keeping house for the college girls, taking joy in their company and entertaining them with her perspectives and memories. During Christmas holidays when the students returned home, she remained at Tabby's Place to tend to the house and cats. Following the girls' graduation, she took all three cats back to her home. Later, she traveled to India to investigate her daughter's mission field.

value: Aunt Euphemia traveled to investigate her daughter's mission field.
unit: After her daughter married and left for the mission field, Aunt Euphemia moved to Portmaris to act as housekeeper for Nell, Honora, Cressy, and Mabel at Tabby's Place. She spent three winters chaperoning and keeping house for the college girls, taking joy in their company and entertaining them with her perspectives and memories. During Christmas holidays when the students returned home, she remained at Tabby's Place to tend to the house and cats. Following the girls' graduation, she took all three cats back to her home. Later, she traveled to India to investigate her daughter's mission field.

label: History
value: Barney drove a double-seated buggy.
unit: Barney drove a double-seated buggy to carry Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke to a concert in Pale Sands, feeling immense pride in traveling alongside Nell, for whom he harbored deep admiration. After his father bestowed the upper farm upon him, Barney wished to marry Nell, but his extreme bashfulness led him to persuade his sister Odette to propose on his behalf. Following Nell's firm refusal, he turned his affections toward Nettie Scobie and married her later that year. The newlyweds were witnessed entering the Gorham Pullen church pew in high spirits on their 'appearing out' Sunday.

label: History
value: Belinda lived at Echo Cottage.
unit: Belinda lived at Echo Cottage as the handmaiden to Miss Rosalind Harcourt, where she was given the designation 'Belinda the Fourth' to follow her three older sisters who had previously served there. She diligently assisted Miss Rosalind with domestic tasks, garden work, and playing along with her imaginative tea parties. When Miss Rosalind grew sick and weary, Belinda privately shared her deep worries with Nell Harcourt. She enthusiastically supported the romantic reunion between Miss Rosalind and Stephen Stanhope, helping Nell polish silver while the proposal took place. Following Miss Rosalind's garden wedding, Belinda moved to Boston in the autumn to continue residing with the newlyweds. Though initially homesick for St. Brendan's Island, she returned to Echo Cottage each summer with the Stanhopes. Eventually, she married a American bricklayer named Tom, though she maintained that she never intended to take a 'Yankee' as a husband. She attended Nell's wedding at Grey Shutters, where she joyously helped toss rice and old shoes as the couple departed.

label: History
value: Cedric came from the United States to Brierley
unit: Cedric came from the United States to Brierley at age ten to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope. Enrolling at Brierley school, he instantly formed a deep friendship with his teacher, Nell Harcourt, who appreciated his imaginative ideas and intellect. During his school years, he defended his American flag in a match with St. Clair Trask, protected younger boys, and courted his classmate Gracie Pullen. Nell introduced him to Miss Rosalind Penrose, with whom he shared imaginative 'dream-people' and formed a warm bond. When his father, Stephen Stanhope, arrived for a surprise visit, Cedric's letters helped facilitate Stephen's reunion and subsequent marriage to Miss Rosalind. Cedric celebrated their wedding by ringing a brass dinner bell that stirred the local echoes. Following the wedding, he moved to Boston with his father and stepmother, returning to Echo Cottage for summer vacations. As he matured into a tall young man of nineteen, he published poetry in magazines and prepared for two years of study abroad in Europe.

label: History
value: Clementine grew up in a strict Episcopalian family.
unit: Clementine grew up in a strict Episcopalian family. At seventeen, her fiancé Martin Crawford was lost at sea, an event that deeply affected her. After her mother's death when Clementine was twenty-five, she and her older sister Harriet swore a mutual oath across their mother's Bible never to marry and to live together for life. She spent years giving music lessons to local children and living quietly in her home on the hill. During an autumn evening at a hidden spring in Fern Hollow, she struck up an acquaintance with the Presbyterian minister, John Ashdown. Their acquaintance turned into a courtship as Ashdown frequented her home, but when he proposed, Clementine reluctantly rejected him in writing due to her binding vow to Harriet. Following the rejection, she visited Portmaris to recover her health. Later, when Harriet wished to marry Lionel Fairlie, Clementine released her sister from the vow. After young Ida Ashdown came to plead with her to marry her father, Clementine sent John Ashdown a note arranging a meeting at the spring, leading to their betrothal.

label: History
value: Cyril returned to Wexcombe
unit: Cyril returned to Wexcombe to finish his Junior year and complete his Arts degree after spending two years in Europe with his ill mother. He met Nell Harcourt in the park during a rainstorm when his umbrella rescued hers, and he subsequently began courting her by sending flowers and poetry. Throughout his time at college, he pursued Nell ardently, writing her sonnets and letters twice a week, leading many to anticipate their engagement. Though his mother and sister Aline were initially cool, his sister Dorothy warmly supported the acquaintance. After Convocation, Cyril proposed to Nell in the harbor park pavilion where they first met. Surprised and deeply hurt when she rejected his proposal, he bade her farewell and declared that no other woman would ever have his affection, though his sister Dorothy noted he would eventually recover as he always did.

label: History
value: Edmund grew up at Hollowmere
unit: Edmund grew up at Hollowmere near Glen St. Agnes as one of the Carrow children. He frequently played with his siblings and local friends in Fern Hollow, a valley he named after a rainbow seemed to land in it. While at school, he was generally viewed as quiet and disinclined toward physical confrontation, preferring to read poetry and share stories with his friends. When Grace Ashdown challenged him to ride a pig through Glen St. Agnes, Edmund accepted to avoid backing down, subsequently taking sole blame for the stunt to protect Grace from criticism. Upon hearing Dan Coyle insult his mother's writing and call Grace derogatory names, Edmund stood up to the bully and agreed to a duel after school. Despite dreading the fight and suffering intense anxiety beforehand, Edmund engaged Dan with wild determination, winning the battle and forcing Dan to retract all his insults. Following the fight, the Rev. John Ashdown commended Edmund for defending the honor of his mother and Grace, giving Edmund the courage to finally face his fear of dental pain and get his troubling tooth extracted.

label: History
value: Flossie attended Brierley school.
unit: Flossie attended Brierley school, where she frequently clashed with Nell Harcourt and challenged her peers to dares, including daring Nell to walk a kitchen roof ridgepole. She won top prize for knitted lace at a local exhibition. Upon entering Miss Thorne's Regent's class, she struggled with arithmetic but managed to pass the Entrance exam by a slim three-point margin. She subsequently attended the Academy, lodging in town and making a name for herself as the most caustic-tongued student at Regent's while continuing to mock her classmates. Later, her home was used to host a send-off celebration for Nell and Hugh Carrow by the B.V.I.S., where she displayed patronizing friendliness toward Nell. She continued her studies at Regent's for an additional year.

label: History
value: Grace moved to Glen St. Agnes
unit: After moving to Glen St. Agnes with her family, Grace enjoyed the freedom of a manse managed without strict domestic training. She frequently shared clothes with guests like Mary Stubbs and engaged in bold antics. When her father faced public gossip, Grace undertook sudden initiatives, such as attempting to clean the house—which accidentally occurred on a Sunday due to a mistaken day count—and marching up to the pulpit platform during church service to give a public explanation. She also challenged Edmund Carrow to ride a pig through Glen St. Agnes and went directly to the feared Lionel Fairlie to persuade him to return to church. When Dan Coyle insulted her, Edmund fought him to defend her honor. To avoid further embarrassment to their father, Grace and her siblings formed the Good-Conduct Club to manage and punish their own misdeeds. After a misunderstanding regarding a grave marker, she published a defiant public clarification in the local newspaper. She eventually sought comfort in Clementine Ainslie, forming a warm bond that welcomed Clementine into her family's life.

label: History
value: Harriet Ainslie grew up in a strict Episcopalian family.
unit: Harriet Ainslie grew up in a strict Episcopalian family. In her youth, she was courted for two years by Lionel Fairlie until a foolish disagreement caused him to marry Dinah Coyle out of spite. Following her mother's death when Clementine was twenty-five, Harriet was overcome by grief and horror at the thought of being left alone, leading her to demand a mutual vow with Clementine upon their mother's Bible to never marry. When John Ashdown began visiting their house and fell in love with Clementine, Harriet frequently engaged him in lively debates on world affairs while keeping a close eye on their interactions to enforce the vow. Upon learning that Ashdown proposed to Clementine, Harriet adamantly refused to release her sister from her oath. Later, after reconnecting with Lionel Fairlie, Harriet found herself courted by him once more. Realizing she wished to marry Lionel, Harriet felt bound by her own logic, eventually consenting to let Clementine marry Ashdown as well.

unit: Harriet Ainslie grew up in a strict Episcopalian family. In her youth, she was courted for two years by Lionel Fairlie until a foolish disagreement caused him to marry Dinah Coyle out of spite. Following her mother's death when Clementine was twenty-five, Harriet was overcome by grief and horror at the thought of being left alone, leading her to demand a mutual vow with Clementine upon their mother's Bible to never marry. When John Ashdown began visiting their house and fell in love with Clementine, Harriet frequently engaged him in lively debates on world affairs while keeping a close eye on their interactions to enforce the vow. Upon learning that Ashdown proposed to Clementine, Harriet adamantly refused to release her sister from her oath. Later, after reconnecting with Lionel Fairlie, Harriet found herself courted by him once more. Realizing she wished to marry Lionel, Harriet felt bound by her own logic, eventually consenting to let Clementine marry Ashdown as well.

label: History
value: Honora attended Regent's Academy.
unit: Honora attended Regent's Academy, where she formed a tight friendship with Nell Harcourt and Mabel Colby. After school, she was assigned to teach at the Delford school and contributed an essay to the Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, she enrolled at Wexcombe alongside Nell, where they roomed together and became close with Cressida Lindsay. With Nell and Mabel, she leased 'Tabby's Place' on Linden Avenue, living under the care of Mabel's Aunt Euphemia. At Wexcombe, she earned Honors in Classics upon graduation. She subsequently married a handsome foreign missionary and relocated to Japan.

label: History
value: Hugh grew up in Brierley.
unit: Hugh grew up in Brierley and attended school there, where he gained a reputation for teasing the girls and competing fiercely for academic top honors with Nell Harcourt. After teasing Nell about her red hair on her first day, a long-standing academic rivalry and rift began between them, though Hugh expressed remorse and sought her friendship. Upon finishing at Regent's as medalist, he taught at Pale Sands to save money for university expenses, relinquishing the local school position to Nell. After entering Wexcombe for college, Hugh studied medicine, eventually earning High Honors in Classics and winning the Cooper Prize, though the intense work led to severe exhaustion and a bout of typhoid fever. Over time, his feud with Nell turned into friendship and later romance. Following their marriage, Hugh took over his great-uncle Dr. David Carrow's medical practice at Glen St. Agnes in Seven Gulls, establishing his home and family there while serving as the local physician.

label: History
value: Ida Ashdown spent her childhood in Glen St. Agnes
unit: Ida Ashdown spent her childhood in Glen St. Agnes following the death of her mother, Cecilia. Raised alongside her siblings Grace, Tobias, and Rupert by their absent-minded father and elderly Aunt Martha, she cherished warm memories of her mother while coping with a dusty home, poor food, and worn clothing. Desiring to improve her family's circumstances, she occasionally tried to clean the manse or mend her father's clothes. When the orphan Mary Stubbs took shelter in Mr. Taylor's barn, Ida showed compassion, housing her at the manse and taking the brave step of visiting Miss Winifred Kerr to persuade her to adopt Mary. She frequently read her mother's old cookbooks to cope with meager meals and envied other children who had mothers, music lessons, or new accessories. Driven by warnings from Mary Stubbs, she developed a deep terror of stepmothers, fearing a second marriage would alienate her father from his children. Despite her fears, after overhearing her father weeping in despair over his love for Clementine Ainslie, Ida conquered her terror and walked to the Ainslie house to beg Clementine to marry her father for his happiness. Her courageous intervention resolved the misunderstanding between Clementine and Rev. Ashdown, paving the way for their engagement.

label: History
value: Isolde returned to Pear Hill from Delford.
unit: After returning to Pear Hill from Delford, Isolde quickly formed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt, swearing a solemn vow of mutual loyalty above a path pretending to be flowing water. The two girls shared a playhouse named Larkrise and spent their time devising creative titles for local spots. Their companionship suffered a brief setback when Isolde became ill after drinking raspberry cordial at Grey Shutters, leading Mrs. Pembroke to misinterpret the event and temporarily forbid them from seeing each other. The misunderstanding was resolved after Nell rescued Posy Fay, allowing their bond to resume.

Their companionship suffered a brief setback when Isolde became ill after drinking raspberry cordial at Grey Shutters, leading Mrs. Pembroke to misinterpret the event and temporarily forbid them from seeing each other. The misunderstanding was resolved after Nell rescued Posy Fay, allowing their bond to resume.

label: History
value: Four years after the death of Cecilia, the Reverend John Knox Ashdown was called to serve as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes.
unit: Four years after the death of his beloved wife Cecilia, the Reverend John Knox Ashdown was called to serve as the pastor of Glen St. Agnes. He moved into the manse with his four children—Grace, Gerald, Tobias, Rupert, and Ida—along with their aged relative, Aunt Martha. Although his brilliant sermons won high praise across the congregation, his severe absent-mindedness and neglect of practical domestic matters often led to forgotten meetings, messy attire, and gossip among the locals. When Mrs. Hector Twiss arrogantly offered to adopt his daughter Ida, John firmly turned her away and was forced to confront his deficiencies as a father. Falling deeply in love with Clementine Ainslie, he proposed to her; though she initially sent a cold written rejection due to a secret vow she had made to her sister, her feelings remained unchanged. After Ida learned of his heartbreak and secretly carried a note from Clementine, the couple reconciled and agreed to marry, which brought a noticeable transformation to John's demeanor and outlook.

He moved into the manse with his four children—Grace, Gerald, Tobias, Rupert, and Ida—along with their aged relative, Aunt Martha. Although his brilliant sermons won high praise across the congregation, his severe absent-mindedness and neglect of practical domestic matters often led to forgotten meetings, messy attire, and gossip among the locals. When Mrs. Hector Twiss arrogantly offered to adopt his daughter Ida, John firmly turned her away and was forced to confront his deficiencies as a father. Falling deeply in love with Clementine Ainslie, he proposed to her; though she initially sent a cold written rejection due to a secret vow she had made to her sister, her feelings remained unchanged. After Ida learned of his heartbreak and secretly carried a note from Clementine, the couple reconciled and agreed to marry, which brought a noticeable transformation to John's demeanor and outlook.

label: History
value: Lionel Fairlie was famous for his reckless driving during his youth.
unit: During his youth, Lionel Fairlie was famous for his reckless driving and wild deeds. He courted Harriet Ainslie for two years, but after a sudden argument, he broke off their relationship and hastily married Dinah Coyle, a meek woman whom he ultimately held in contempt for her lack of spirit. Following an issue where he felt cheated in a cow deal by a member of the church session, Lionel quit attending church altogether for twenty years, insisting his wife restrict her donations while forcing him to remain an unobservant pagan. Ten years after his wife's passing, Grace Ashdown visited his farm to ask for financial support and church attendance on behalf of her father, the minister. Though he initially bellowed at her, Grace's spirited retaliation won his admiration, leading him to agree to attend service once a month and contribute one hundred dollars annually to the minister's stipend. Upon returning to church, Lionel saw Harriet Ainslie for the first time in two decades and fell deeply in love with her once more. He began actively courting her, visiting her regularly, and debating with her. He eventually approached Harriet's sister Clementine to secure her release of a youth vow that blocked Harriet from marrying. When Harriet was finally free to accept him, Lionel was overjoyed at the prospect of their upcoming marriage.

He courted Harriet Ainslie for two years, but after a sudden argument, he broke off their relationship and hastily married Dinah Coyle, a meek woman whom he ultimately held in contempt for her lack of spirit. Following an issue where he felt cheated in a cow deal by a member of the church session, Lionel quit attending church altogether for twenty years, insisting his wife restrict her donations while forcing him to remain an unobservant pagan. Ten years after his wife's passing, Grace Ashdown visited his farm to ask for financial support and church attendance on behalf of her father, the minister. Though he initially bellowed at her, Grace's spirited retaliation won his admiration, leading him to agree to attend service once a month and contribute one hundred dollars annually to the minister's stipend. Upon returning to church, Lionel saw Harriet Ainslie for the first time in two decades and fell deeply in love with her once more. He began actively courting her, visiting her regularly, and debating with her. He eventually approached Harriet's sister Clementine to secure her release of a youth vow that blocked Harriet from marrying. When Harriet was finally free to accept him, Lionel was overjoyed at the prospect of their upcoming marriage.

label: History
value: Kit was born at the small house of dreams near the harbour.
unit: Kit was born at the small house of dreams near the harbour, the eldest son of Dr. Carrow and Nell Carrow. Prior to his death, Captain Saul Garrick willed him a collection of unusual curiosities. As a baby, his mother resolved never to use baby talk with him, though she quickly broke her own rule. In his childhood, his family moved from the house of dreams to Hollowmere in the Glen. At the age of eight, he strongly protested being called 'Little Kit', prompting his mother to stop using the nickname around him, though Tabitha continued to do so. Kit grew into a solid, dependable leader among his peers at school, excelling in sports and outdoor activities. He spent much of his youth playing in Fern Hollow, fishing for trout, collecting curiosities in the attic, and gathering wild flowers for his mother. In his early teens, he suggested the creation of a Good-Conduct Club to assist the manse children. At thirteen, Kit stayed after school to study for the entrance examination at Regent's Academy, ultimately departing for Port Marlow to attend the academy.

label: History
value: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls.
unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls, enduring a tragic youth marked by the sudden death of her brother Julian and the suicide of her father. Despite these horrors, she pursued an education at Regent's Academy and taught at the Glen school. To save her family farm from foreclosure, she surrendered her dreams and married Rufus Vane. Shortly after her mother's death, Rufus departed for sea; years later, Captain Saul brought back a brain-damaged man believed to be Rufus, whom Lorna faithfully nursed for eleven years in near poverty.

Despite these horrors, she pursued an education at Regent's Academy and taught at the Glen school. To save her family farm from foreclosure, she surrendered her dreams and married Rufus Vane. Shortly after her mother's death, Rufus departed for sea; years later, Captain Saul brought back a brain-damaged man believed to be Rufus, whom Lorna faithfully nursed for eleven years in near poverty.

value: Upon the arrival of Nell and Hugh Carrow, Lorna gradually formed a friendship with Nell.
unit: Upon the arrival of Nell and Hugh Carrow, Lorna gradually formed a close but complex friendship with Nell. When Lorna hosted author Adrian Treleaven as a summer lodger, she secretly fell in love with him, though she felt constrained by her marital ties. Later, she agreed to let Hugh arrange a surgical operation in Montreal for her incapacitated companion. The surgery restored his memory, revealing that he was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, and that the real Rufus Vane had died of yellow fever in Cuba thirteen years prior. Unbound and free, Lorna returned to Seven Gulls, took up temporary residence with Nell, and rekindled her connection with Adrian Treleaven.

value: Lucy is well-behaved.

However, she is easily frightened by things like dark rooms, ghosts, or cows, and tends to follow rules and lessons like a small automaton without much imagination. Though prim and unvarying, she is deeply proper, moral, and attentive to etiquette.

label: History
value: Lucy's mother died.
unit: Following the death of her mother, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were brought by Thirza to live at Grey Shutters under her and Nell's care. From an early age, Lucy proved to be extremely polite and well-mannered, though she was frequently subject to her brother Robin's antics, such as having her hair pulled or being tricked into standing in a pigpen and getting drenched. When Robin locked her in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse, she wept with fear until Nell rescued her. At seven years old, she began attending school alongside Robin, where she enjoyed her studies but was frightened of dark spaces after hearing ghost stories from a classmate. When a sudden, violent hail storm struck Grey Shutters, Lucy remained remarkably composed while sitting beside Nell. As she grew older, she inherited Nell's former porch room when Nell married, showing great responsibility in helping care for young children during the wedding. By seventeen years of age, she began receiving romantic attention from Ralph Pullen.

label: History
value: Mabel attended Regent's Academy.
unit: Mabel attended Regent's Academy, where she formed a close bond with Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis. During her second year, she won the beauty prize among her classmates. After finishing at Regent's, she worked continuously as a schoolteacher. Later, she reunited with Nell and Honora to study at Wexcombe, renting Tabby's Place alongside them, Cressida Lindsay, and her Aunt Euphemia, who took charge of housekeeping. After finishing her studies and achieving a respectable overall performance at Convocation, she eventually moved to Vancouver to pursue her teaching career.

After finishing at Regent's, she worked continuously as a schoolteacher. Later, she reunited with Nell and Honora to study at Wexcombe, renting Tabby's Place alongside them, Cressida Lindsay, and her Aunt Euphemia, who took charge of housekeeping. After finishing her studies and achieving a respectable overall performance at Convocation, she eventually moved to Vancouver to pursue her teaching career.

value: Mary is lively.
unit: Mary is lively, outspoken, proud, and inclined to boast about herself. Subjected to severe physical abuse and neglect in her early childhood, she retains a deep fear of punishment and ghost stories, which she tells with dramatic flair. Though sometimes quick-tempered, jealous, and prone to lecturing or sharing upsetting gossip, she is intensely loyal to her friends and capable of genuine remorse and affection.

label: History
value: Mary ran away from Mrs. Grimble
unit: After running away from the abusive Mrs. Grimble across the harbor, Mary hid in a barn near the manse at Glen St. Agnes without food for days. She surrendered to the manse children, who fed her and gave her clothes. After learning of Mrs. Grimble's sudden death from heart disease, Mary feared she might be sent back to the Hopetown asylum. Mr. Ashdown comforted her in his study, and Ida Ashdown pleaded with Winifred Kerr to adopt Mary. Mrs. Kerr took Mary into her household, where Mary proved to be an exceptionally energetic domestic worker and pupil. She became a constant playmate of the manse and Hollowmere children in Fern Hollow, frequently sharing spine-tingling ghost stories, giving advice, and inadvertently causing alarm with her warnings about stepmothers.

label: History
value: Nell was sent to live at Grey Shutters with Thirza Abernethy.
unit: After being sent to live at Grey Shutters with Thirza Abernethy, Nell quickly formed a deep bond with her best friend, Isolde Pembroke. At school in Brierley, she got into frequent scrapes due to her vivid imagination and quick temper, including breaking a slate over Hugh Carrow's head after he teased her red hair, and accidentally dyeing her hair green before a major event. Winning the prestigious Avery Prize, she decided to defer college to teach school in Delford and Brierley so she could care for Thirza during her failing eyesight. Later, she attended college, where she began publishing short fiction stories. Although pursued by Cyril and Barney Pullen, she declined their proposals, realizing her true sentiments. Eventually, she married Dr. Carrow and survived a severe, prolonged illness following the birth of her son, Harcourt.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters
unit: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Intending to adopt a young orphan boy to assist with farm work, he traveled to the Alder River station in June, only to discover that an orphan girl, Nell, had been sent by mistake instead. Reluctant to leave her stranded, Obed brought her home and immediately grew fond of her lively conversation, persuading Thirza to let her stay. He formed a warm, affectionate bond with Nell, frequently defending her against punishments and indulging her wishes, including buying her a fashionable new dress for Christmas. Over the following years, he took immense pride in Nell's academic achievements, including her winning the Avery scholarship. As his health declined and financial anxieties mounted over the instability of the local bank holding their savings, Obed collapsed from a sudden heart ailment at his doorway and passed away, being buried shortly after in the Brierley cemetery.

Intending to adopt a young orphan boy to assist with farm work, he traveled to the Alder River station in June, only to discover that an orphan girl, Nell, had been sent by mistake instead. Reluctant to leave her stranded, Obed brought her home and immediately grew fond of her lively conversation, persuading Thirza to let her stay. He formed a warm, affectionate bond with Nell, frequently defending her against punishments and indulging her wishes, including buying her a fashionable new dress for Christmas. Over the following years, he took immense pride in Nell's academic achievements, including her winning the Avery scholarship. As his health declined and financial anxieties mounted over the instability of the local bank holding their savings, Obed collapsed from a sudden heart ailment at his doorway and passed away, being buried shortly after in the Brierley cemetery.

label: History
value: Odette grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette grew up in Brierley and attended school alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. She joined the Regent's class to study for the Entrance exam, qualifying as a teacher at Regent's Academy. During her school years, she was a member of the all-female Story Club and the Brierley Village Improvement Society (B.V.I.S.), serving on its hall renovation committee. She taught at the Stonebridge school before returning to take over the Brierley school after Nell's departure. Later, she accepted a teaching position out on the western prairies. During a winter holiday back in Brierley, she attempted to propose marriage to Nell on behalf of her bashful brother Barney, which Nell declined. While teaching in the West, she met and became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman from Winnipeg. They married in Brierley, attended by a large family gathering, and went to Europe for their honeymoon before taking up residence in a mansion in Winnipeg.

During her school years, she was a member of the all-female Story Club and the Brierley Village Improvement Society (B.V.I.S.), serving on its hall renovation committee. She taught at the Stonebridge school before returning to take over the Brierley school after Nell's departure. Later, she accepted a teaching position out on the western prairies. During a winter holiday back in Brierley, she attempted to propose marriage to Nell on behalf of her bashful brother Barney, which Nell declined. While teaching in the West, she met and became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman from Winnipeg. They married in Brierley, attended by a large family gathering, and went to Europe for their honeymoon before taking up residence in a mansion in Winnipeg.

label: History
value: Opal attended Brierley school
unit: Opal attended Brierley school, where she shared desks and games with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen. She joined the school's Story Club, participated in recitations and concerts, and played games along the pond. She later progressed to the Regent's class and attended Regent's Academy in Port Marlow. After completing her studies, she secured a position teaching at the Delford school. During her adolescence, Opal was constantly surrounded by suitors, rejecting Nelson Atkins after realizing he copied his proposal from an etiquette book. She later contracted a severe chest congestion during the winter, which developed into galloping consumption. Forced to stop teaching, she harbored hopes of resuming her career at Pale Sands school. As her condition deteriorated throughout the summer, she shared an emotional conversation in her garden with Nell Harcourt, confessing her terror of dying young. Shortly after, Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep and was buried in the Brierley cemetery.

She joined the school's Story Club, participated in recitations and concerts, and played games along the pond. She later progressed to the Regent's class and attended Regent's Academy in Port Marlow. After completing her studies, she secured a position teaching at the Delford school. During her adolescence, Opal was constantly surrounded by suitors, rejecting Nelson Atkins after realizing he copied his proposal from an etiquette book. She later contracted a severe chest congestion during the winter, which developed into galloping consumption. Forced to stop teaching, she harbored hopes of resuming her career at Pale Sands school. As her condition deteriorated throughout the summer, she shared an emotional conversation in her garden with Nell Harcourt, confessing her terror of dying young. Shortly after, Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep and was buried in the Brierley cemetery.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer bought Mr. Bell's farm in Brierley.
unit: After buying Mr. Bell's farm in Brierley, Mr. Pettifer quickly established a reputation as a solitary, stingy crank who kept his own house, maintained irregular eating habits, avoided washing dishes, and kept a foul-mouthed parrot named Nutmeg. He frequently clashed with neighbor Nell Harcourt over her cow straying into his oatfield. However, when Nell accidentally sold his cow and came to apologize with a cake, he forgave her cordially, took her cow in trade, and formed an enduring friendship with her. He routinely provided advice and honest critiques on Nell's teaching methods and writing endeavors. Following the death of Nutmeg by a lightning strike, a prank letter in a newspaper prompted his estranged wife, Emily, to arrive in Brierley. Reunited with Emily, Mr. Pettifer adopted a cleaner, more orderly lifestyle and regularly attended church, while maintaining an armed neutrality toward local busybody Agatha Sowerby. He was later invited to attend Nell's wedding.

label: History
value: Ezra Hale studied theology at St. Columbia
unit: While studying theology at St. Columbia, Ezra Hale spent a summer in charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church, where he met Cressida Lindsay. Despite initial hesitation about entering the ministry, he embraced his calling and delivered moving sermons at the village church. During his studies, he visited Cressy at Tabby's Place in Wexcombe and eventually proposed to her. Following his graduation from St. Columbia, he took charge of a small mission church in the Tanner Street slums. He married Cressy the following June, after which they went on a saunter through the land of Evangeline before taking up residence in the slums. Together they had children, and he later attended the wedding of Hugh and Nell, offering a beautiful wedding prayer during the service.

Despite initial hesitation about entering the ministry, he embraced his calling and delivered moving sermons at the village church. During his studies, he visited Cressy at Tabby's Place in Wexcombe and eventually proposed to her. Following his graduation from St. Columbia, he took charge of a small mission church in the Tanner Street slums. He married Cressy the following June, after which they went on a saunter through the land of Evangeline before taking up residence in the slums. Together they had children, and he later attended the wedding of Hugh and Nell, offering a beautiful wedding prayer during the service.

label: History
value: Robin's mother died in East Welby.
unit: Following the death of his sick mother in East Welby, Robin and his twin sister Lucy were brought to Grey Shutters by Thirza Abernethy, their third cousin once removed. Initially, Robin proved to be an overwhelming handful, constantly indulging in wild pranks, lying to avoid trouble, and terrorizing the household by putting a toad in Thirza's bed and locking Lucy inside a building. Through the gentle guidance and affection of Nell, Robin's behavior gradually improved, although his mischievous nature frequently resurfaced. When his uncle Richard Farrow died, a trust fund was established under Thirza's care to support Robin and Lucy. As Robin grew older, he entered school, made friends like Milty Gammon, and developed a keen interest in agriculture, eventually seeking permission to help manage the farm.

label: History
value: Rufus Vane spent his summers sailing.
unit: Rufus Vane spent his summers sailing and his winters clerking in his father Abner's store at the Glen. Becoming obsessed with Lorna Ainslie despite her constant rejections, he forced her into marriage at seventeen by threatening that his father would foreclose on her mother Rose's farm mortgage. Following their wedding, Rufus and Lorna lived on the Ainslie farm through the winter. By spring, after Rose passed away, Rufus grew tired of domestic life and left for Nova Scotia and Cuba. He contracted yellow fever in Cuba and died there thirteen years prior to the events at Seven Gulls. For twelve years, his local community mistakenly believed his surviving double cousin, Laurence Vane—who had suffered severe brain trauma and loss of memory—was Rufus returned home.

value: Rupert lived at the Glen St. Agnes manse
unit: Rupert lived at the Glen St. Agnes manse under the care of his father and elderly Aunt Martha. He spent much of his time exploring, playing in the graveyard with his siblings, and keeping unusual animal companions, such as snakes and insects, which led him to sleep in his old crib rather than share a bed. On one occasion, he retrieved a snake from the cellar using a forked stick. During a frightful experience in Fern Hollow, he fled from what he believed was a ghost, prompting his brother Tobias to assign him a penalty watch in the cemetery until midnight. Remaining on Hezekiah Pollock's tombstone in a cold rainstorm to fulfill his punishment, Rupert contracted severe double pneumonia and nearly died before recovering with the aid of Dr. Carrow and local care. Later, after putting a live eel in Mrs. Carr's buggy, his father prepared to whip him for the prank but proved unable to go through with the lashing upon looking into Rupert's eyes. When his father planned a four-week wedding trip, arrangements were made for Rupert to stay at Elder Clow's household.

label: Quotes
value: > Time for breakfast now. It is my belief that some food and drink will be welcomed by us all. Instruct young Mrs. Doctor to be entirely free of concern—Tabitha is taking charge. Instruct her to occupy her thoughts solely with her infant.

label: Quotes
value: > An old maid I may be, yet you do not catch ME speaking ill of men. They suit me fine. Had the opportunity arisen, I would gladly have wed one.

label: Quotes
value: > Mrs. Dr. dear, I brought him into this world every bit as much as you. The baby belongs to me every bit as much as he belongs to you.

label: Quotes
value: > Writing poetry has never brought about any benefit in my experience, and I trust and petition that that precious boy will leave the inclination behind. Should he fail to do so—it remains for us to observe what a cod-liver oil emulsion can accomplish.

label: Quotes
value: > Mrs. Dr. dear, I do not question that her decision is quite practical, yet personally I have constantly held the opinion that should I ever get wed, I would choose the veil and white to feel more like a bride.

label: History
value: Tabitha Pratt began working as a general servant.
unit: Tabitha Pratt began working as a general servant for Nell Carrow at the small house of dreams. Despite initial suspicion from Thirza Abernethy, Tabitha quickly formed a deep, devoted affection for Nell, whom she affectionately called 'young Mrs. Doctor'. She faithfully managed the household during Nell's illness after the loss of her first baby and stayed on through subsequent seasons. When Dr. Carrow purchased the Varley property at Hollowmere, Tabitha moved with the family, delighted to be closer to society in the Glen. She helped raise all of Nell's children, forming an exceptionally strong maternal bond with young Harcourt during Nell's prolonged illness following his birth. At Hollowmere, Tabitha remained the commanding authority of the household, keeping up with local Glen gossip, attending Presbytarian church affairs, and fearlessly protecting the home.

label: History
value: Tessa Carrow grew up at Hollowmere
unit: Tessa Carrow grew up at Hollowmere as the youngest child of Nell and Dr. Hugh Carrow, routinely thrashed by Tabitha whenever it was believed her spiritual well-being required it. She was given the task of delivering a basket of early strawberries to the manse, with strict instructions from Tabitha to give them only to Aunt Martha or Mr. Ashdown. Upon arriving at the manse hill, she was confronted by Mary Stubbs, who attempted to take the basket. Tessa steadfastly refused to hand it over, which provoked Mary to mock her vanity, perform an uncanny dance, and chase her down the Glen street while brandishing a dried codfish. Terrified, Tessa fled and dropped the basket, crushing the strawberries, before tripping into a mud puddle. Miss Winifred rescued her from the ordeal and carried her home, though Tessa's pride and fine garments were severely ruined by the event. She later studied her primers on the veranda with Tabitha and Harcourt, and joined her siblings on a visit to Julian and Damaris Treleaven at the House of Dreams.

Tessa steadfastly refused to hand it over, which provoked Mary to mock her vanity, perform an uncanny dance, and chase her down the Glen street while brandishing a dried codfish. Terrified, Tessa fled and dropped the basket, crushing the strawberries, before tripping into a mud puddle. Miss Winifred rescued her from the ordeal and carried her home, though Tessa's pride and fine garments were severely ruined by the event. She later studied her primers on the veranda with Tabitha and Harcourt, and joined her siblings on a visit to Julian and Damaris Treleaven at the House of Dreams.

label: Personality
value: Thirza is rigid.
unit: Thirza is rigid, reserved, and unyielding in her moral sense, holding high expectations for neatness and decorum. She strongly dislikes emotional displays or translucent expressions of affection, considering intense feelings improper to exhibit publicly. Despite her stern, austere demeanor and sharp tongue, she harbors deep capacity for affection and hidden softness. Over time, particularly through her relationship with Nell, her sharp temperament mellows into a gentler maturity.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters.
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived a quiet, structured life at Grey Shutters in Brierley alongside her brother Obed. Expecting to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to work the farm, an error resulted in Obed bringing home Nell Harcourt instead. Although initially surprised and skeptical, Thirza permitted Nell to stay and raised her with strict discipline and growing affection. Following Obed's death, Thirza contemplated selling Grey Shutters due to financial and sight difficulties, but Nell chose to stay in Brierley to preserve the home. Later, Thirza agreed to take in twin orphans, Robin and Lucy Farrow, raising them to adulthood. Following the passing of her neighbor Thomas Sowerby, Thirza invited Mrs. Agatha Sowerby to live with her at Grey Shutters. In her old age, Thirza remains living at Grey Shutters, warmly receiving visits from Nell's children.

unit: Thirza Abernethy lived a quiet, structured life at Grey Shutters in Brierley alongside her brother Obed. Expecting to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to work the farm, an error resulted in Obed bringing home Nell Harcourt instead. Although initially surprised and skeptical, Thirza permitted Nell to stay and raised her with strict discipline and growing affection. Following Obed's death, Thirza contemplated selling Grey Shutters due to financial and sight difficulties, but Nell chose to stay in Brierley to preserve the home. Later, Thirza agreed to take in twin orphans, Robin and Lucy Farrow, raising them to adulthood. Following the passing of her neighbor Thomas Sowerby, Thirza invited Mrs. Agatha Sowerby to live with her at Grey Shutters. In her old age, Thirza remains living at Grey Shutters, warmly receiving visits from Nell's children.

label: History
value: Agnes Thorne was hired as a teacher
unit: Agnes Thorne was hired as the first female teacher for the school in Brierley. Upon her arrival, she introduced dynamic educational methods including biweekly recitation programs, field days in the forest, daily physical culture exercises, and composition training, earning the devotion of students like Nell Harcourt and Isolde. During her first autumn, she organized a Christmas Night concert with the students to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Later, she established an after-school preparation class for pupils aiming to take the Regent's entrance examination. Though offered a teaching position in her home district, Miss Thorne chose to remain at Brierley for a second year out of deep interest in her students. She guided her Regent's class through rigorous preparation and administered practice exams before seeing her tenure at Brierley end when the term concluded at the end of June. During exam week, she accompanied her candidates to the Academy to ensure they were settled. Later, she visited the Harcourt home as a guest on occasions such as dinner parties.

label: History
value: Winifred resided in Seven Gulls.
unit: Winifred resided in Seven Gulls, where she established a reputation for her skilled needlework, excellent baking, and vehement disdain for men and Methodists. Upon meeting Nell Carrow, she quickly recognized her as a like-minded spirit and formed a close friendship with her and her husband Hugh, frequently visiting their house and engaging in verbal sparring matches with Captain Saul Garrick. She acted as a protective confidante and closest friend to Lorna Vane, providing guidance during Lorna's personal trials. After staying unmarried for many years, she surprised her friends by agreeing to marry her longtime suitor, Ambrose Kerr, though locals continued to call her Miss Winifred for over a decade. In later years, she took in an orphaned girl named Mary Stubbs to raise her in a good home, and she actively looked out for the well-being of the minister's children at the Glen manse.
